1.mascotDialogue: Same values, two views — a tree for the ordering rule, an array for how she actually sits in memory. parent(i) is (i minus one) over two. That's the whole address book right there.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 3's the bridge between array and tree — any index's parent is always (i-1)/2, integer division. Line 4's the min-heap rule herself — stop the second the parent's already smaller or equal.

3.mascotDialogue: Hover index 4 in the array — watch her tree node light up as a child of index 1. Same data, two windows onto it.

4.mascotDialogue: Both the array cell and the tree node light up the same broken colour at once — 'cause it's one violation, just seen two ways.
